risks: Root wave0 may change inspected bytes after hashes were sampled; this is working-copy source evidence, not revision-bound feature proof.
Overwriting the already-existing normative handler path destroys local repository receipt functionality and conflicts with integration ownership.
Reusing transient request cancellation for durable runs makes repeated/after-restart cancellation non-idempotent; changing the wire contract without coordinated consumers breaks wave0.
Per-run/per-policy locks permit duplicate writers in the same canonical output namespace; TTL-only takeover permits stale writers to publish.
Routing through current operation() for all status calls demands a live branch/root and can hide persistent failure/stale state when disconnected.
Workspace-only pushes can leak repository identifiers to unauthorized peers in the same workspace; no actor/source grants are exposed directly by current RequestContext.
Published shared paths omit typed event and public DTO/export/lifecycle seams; a compile-clean job implementation is insufficient without owner-approved shared integration.
Registry readiness metadata is not an executor/runtime/license receipt; search capability and checkpoint/resume behavior cannot be simulated to satisfy full DoD.
indexVerifiedSnapshotFiles only processes commit-backed files. Dirty snapshot bytes must not gain a false parent-commit citation or silently lose coverage.
Generic source FTS records are not exact code-snapshot results and may be unavailable under Electron Node; do not add a second index or call undocumented upstream endpoints.
Project policy/root changes and deletion can race with job publication; reauthorization plus journal fence is required before commit and event projection.
All five published verification scenarios apply to every DoD row; source inspection alone leaves fullFeatureDoD NOT_VERIFIED.
